summary: Steel fire tower with two cabs on Elk Neck State Forest, probably built in the late 1940s; the state proposed demolition in 2025 and I found no record it happened.

facts.design: Steel tower with two cabs, one above the other
facts.status_note: The state proposed demolishing it in 2025; I found no record that this has happened.

visit.trail_note: A gravel road about a mile long runs from McKinneytown Road to the tower site.

events.note: Deed date for the tower site; the survey gives the installation as probably the late 1940s
Maryland Historical Trust found demolition would have an adverse effect; comments requested by September 30, 2025

notes_for_editor: Status: the DNR notice proposes demolition with comments requested by September 30, 2025; my searches found no later update, so the tower may or may not still stand. Verify with Elk Neck State Forest before publishing a status. Second-cab attribution conflicts: the survey says possibly early joint DNR and ATT use; the notice says Western Union added it in the 1950s. Both are cited and the story says the sources disagree. The survey calls ATT by its initials only, so the story does not describe it as a company. The survey table gives 110 ft, but the survey does not say where that height is measured, so no height_m is recorded. Condition data date from the survey as of December 2006. The easternuslookouts.weebly.com Black Hill page has a title only and no text. The Cecil County history article returned HTTP 403 and is not used. Events: the 2025 year is inferred from the comment deadline in the notice.
